summary: Six new tests added in commit ab2c518 cover all six TDD anchors named in tasks/12.md with matching method names. AC16 three-way contract, AC17 $.code-null + joined-message regex, AC18 Max-Age + HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite for both rememberMe branches, and TC5 bean-type assertion are all pinned with strong assertions that would fail on regression of the named invariants. The deviation on TC11 XSRF-TOKEN co-emission is structurally justified (Spring Security TestCsrfTokenRepository substitution + CookieCsrfTokenRepository skip-when-present behaviour), documented in javadoc, and compensated by SecurityConfigTest.csrfCookie_writtenOnSafeVerbRequest on the cookie-write path. Helpers (parseSetCookie / parseSetCookieHeaderFor / assertCookieAttributesMatchConfig) are correctly scoped, case-insensitive, and config-driven so tests track application(-test).properties drift. Isolation is sound (cleanState/cleanAndSeed wipe users / events / sessions / Redis / Mailpit per test). Two minor findings: (1) the rememberMeTrue test method name advertises XSRF co-emission that the body intentionally does not assert — rename to remove the false advertisement; (2) parseSetCookieHeaderFor returns the first matching Set-Cookie header, which could mask a session-fixation rotation flow that emits a clear-old cookie before the new one — defense-in-depth to assert exactly one matching SESSION header would harden the test.

findings.issue: Method name login_rememberMeTrue_setsAllSessionCookieAttributes_andCoEmitsXsrfToken advertises XSRF co-emission verification that the test body intentionally does NOT perform (per the javadoc on lines 597-609, TC11 is shifted to SecurityConfigTest.csrfCookie_writtenOnSafeVerbRequest). A reader scanning test method names sees coverage that the implementation does not actually provide — this is a false-coverage signal a future maintainer could miss.
findings.recommendation: Rename the method to drop the `_andCoEmitsXsrfToken` suffix so the name reflects what is asserted, e.g. `login_rememberMeTrue_setsAllSessionCookieAttributes` (matching the rememberMeFalse counterpart on line 635). Keep the existing javadoc intact — it correctly documents why TC11 is covered elsewhere. Alternatively, add a single `andExpect(cookie().exists("XSRF-TOKEN"))` style probe to attempt the assertion and let it confirm or refute the structural-impossibility claim. Method name and test surface should agree.

findings.issue: parseSetCookieHeaderFor returns the FIRST Set-Cookie header whose value starts with `cookieName + "="`. AuthService.openSession() calls httpRequest.changeSessionId() (line 609 of AuthService), and the Spring Session servlet flow can emit a clear-old-SESSION-cookie (`SESSION=; Max-Age=0; ...`) immediately followed by the new SESSION cookie. If this ever happens, the AC18 Max-Age assertions would be made against the wrong (clear) cookie — Max-Age=0 string would not match Long.toString(2592000), so the test would fail loudly rather than silently pass; but if the order ever flips, the test could pass against a stale cookie and miss the regression. This is a defense-in-depth concern, not an active bug — the current login flow on this stack appears to emit a single SESSION cookie per response.
findings.recommendation: Either: (a) change parseSetCookieHeaderFor to collect ALL Set-Cookie headers matching the name and assert exactly one, picking that one explicitly; or (b) add a precondition in both AC18 tests counting `response.getHeaders("Set-Cookie").stream().filter(h -> h.startsWith("SESSION=")).count()` and asserting it equals 1 before parsing. Concrete shape: `long sessionCookieCount = response.getHeaders("Set-Cookie").stream().filter(h -> h.startsWith("SESSION=")).count(); assertThat(sessionCookieCount).as("exactly one SESSION Set-Cookie header expected").isEqualTo(1L);` placed before the parseSetCookieHeaderFor call.

notes: AuthControllerIT.cleanState (line 90-101) wipes users, events, Redis keys (all *), sessions collection, and Mailpit messages — covers every cross-test surface the new tests touch.

ProfileControllerIT.cleanAndSeed (line 53-69) wipes users, events, sessions and reseeds the canonical USER_ID user. The new tests use the same seeded user (profile@test.com) for login or operate under @WithMockAppUser — no extra teardown needed.
New tests use distinct user emails (rmt@, rmf@, sess-B/sess-other-user as session IDs, pre-flip-session as session ID) — no email/sessionId collisions with pre-existing tests in either file.
AC18 tests' configured-attribute assertions are read-only (no mutation) so they cannot leak state.

deviationEvaluation.deviation: AC18 XSRF-TOKEN co-emission on the same login response is NOT asserted in login_rememberMeTrue_... test
deviationEvaluation.rationale: The javadoc at AuthControllerIT.java:597-609 lists three structural reasons: (1) without .with(csrf()) the POST returns 403; (2) with .with(csrf()) the SecurityMockMvc post-processor swaps the real CookieCsrfTokenRepository for a TestCsrfTokenRepository, so the production save path never runs; (3) on a real round-trip CookieCsrfTokenRepository.RepositoryDeferredCsrfToken only saves when loadToken returned null — once a valid XSRF-TOKEN cookie is present in the request, saveToken is correctly skipped. These constraints are real and rooted in Spring Security test infrastructure design. Coverage of the cookie-write path is preserved by SecurityConfigTest.csrfCookie_writtenOnSafeVerbRequest on a fresh anonymous GET /health, which exercises the same CookieCsrfTokenRepository.saveToken branch. The deviation is documented in javadoc and decisions.md per the task post-completion checklist. This matches test-master Category 5 / 6 principles: avoid excessive test ceremony to assert against a stubbed surface; assert against the real code path where it actually fires.
deviationEvaluation.concern: The method name still advertises the assertion that the body skips (see finding #1) — separate from the deviation being technically sound.

concerns.concern: findFirst() on principal-matching sessions document assumes the login created exactly one document for USER_ID. Spring Session uses 32+ char UUIDs as session ids — collision with the literal 'sess-B' or 'sess-other-user' seeded later is astronomically unlikely. The seedSession(sess-B) call happens AFTER currentSessionId is captured, so even a (vanishingly improbable) UUID-vs-literal collision would surface as a test failure rather than a silent pass.
concerns.mitigation: No change needed — current shape is correct. A pedantic hardening would be `assertThat(sessions).hasSize(1)` before findFirst, but the existing orElseThrow lambda effectively performs that check.

concerns.concern: parseSetCookieHeaderFor returns first matching Set-Cookie header — see finding #2 for the session-fixation rotation edge case.

flakinessAssessment.evidence: Task post-completion checklist (lines 184 of tasks/12.md) requires 3x sequential passing runs and the commit log states this was performed. The cookie-shape assertions are deterministic (DefaultCookieSerializer source path is single-branch per Max-Age value); BSON fixture insert is deterministic via insertOne; Spring Session session id generation is per-request, not order-dependent.

notes: Splits on `;`, trims segments, skips empty segments — handles trailing semicolons defensively.
Lowercases keys for case-insensitive lookup — correctly handles SameSite vs samesite header-attribute case variation.
Stores name and value under reserved __name/__value keys so flag attributes (HttpOnly, Secure) parsed as empty strings cannot collide with the cookie name/value. Reasonable defensive design.
Scoped private static — testable in isolation if needed but not over-exposed.
Iterates response.getHeaders("Set-Cookie") and returns first match by cookieName + "=" prefix.
See finding #2 — first-match semantics could mask a clear-then-set rotation. Not currently a defect because the live flow appears to emit one SESSION cookie per response.
Shared between both AC18 tests so the configured-value invariant is checked uniformly.
Reads @Value-bound cfgCookieHttpOnly / cfgCookieSecure / cfgCookieSameSite — assertions track application(-test).properties drift automatically, satisfying the tech-spec guidance.
SameSite compared case-insensitively per RFC 6265bis — correct.
Distinguishes 'absent' from 'present' for flag attributes via containsKey — correct.
AC17 message regex `^email: .+(, .+: .+)*$` allows locale variation in default-message text but pins the joiner shape — the right balance between brittleness and regression detection.

AC18 Max-Age expected value is computed from @Value-bound rememberMeDays * 86400 rather than hardcoded 2592000 — config drift surfaces explicitly without breaking the assertion. Comparison uses Long.toString to match the raw header byte-shape.

AC16(b) currentSessionId is captured from the live sessions collection AFTER login, then asserted post-change-password — this is the litmus-test-strong shape: if ProfileService.terminateAllSessionsExcept were to omit the `_id != currentSessionId` clause, currentCount would be 0 and the test would fail loudly.

TC5 isInstanceOf is the right granularity — equals(...) on RememberMeCookieSerializer.class would be wrong (subclass identity), instanceof handles future subclasses correctly while still catching DefaultCookieSerializer regression.

Litmus test passed for all six tests: removing the core production-side line (terminate-by-principal delete; MethodArgumentNotValidException handler; RememberMeCookieSerializer.writeCookieValue Max-Age branch; RememberMeCookieSerializer @Bean registration) would cause the corresponding test to fail.
